Query Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL as the signed-in user

Source: R/backend__cosmos.R
oauth_db_cosmos_api.Rd

Read documents with each visitor's Microsoft Entra access token and Cosmos DB data-plane permissions. Queries use the NoSQL HTTPS API; no database driver or Azure SDK is needed.

Usage

oauth_db_cosmos_api(
  authorization,
  url,
  database,
  container,
  target = "cosmos",
  required_scopes = character(),
  min_valid_for = 60,
  timeout = 300,
  page_size = 1000L,
  api_version = "2020-07-15",
  ca_bundle = NULL,
  session = shiny::getDefaultReactiveDomain()
)

Arguments

authorization

Function providing the visitor's current sign-in authorization. Pass auth$connection from shinyOAuth without parentheses. To select a saved account, use a function calling auth$connection(id).

url

Cosmos DB account HTTPS origin, such as "https://example.documents.azure.com".

database

Database ID.

container

Container ID.

target

Name of the service token to use in your shinyOAuth client. Named targets let one sign-in obtain tokens for different services. NULL uses the client's default token.

required_scopes

Additional OAuth permissions to check before use. Request them on the shinyOAuth client first; this check doesn't request consent or grant database privileges.

min_valid_for

Minimum remaining token lifetime, in seconds, when obtaining a token. Use 0 to accept any unexpired token.

timeout

Total seconds allowed for an operation and all its pages.

page_size

Maximum items requested per page, or -1 for the service default. A page can contain fewer items, including none.

api_version

Cosmos DB REST service version.

ca_bundle

Optional trusted CA certificate bundle path.

session

The visitor's Shiny session. Usually inferred when you create the helper inside server().

Value

A session-bound client with these methods:

  • $query(sql, parameters = list(), partition_key = NULL, raw = FALSE) collects all pages and returns a data frame.

  • $query_page(sql, parameters = list(), partition_key = NULL, continuation = NULL, session_token = NULL) returns one page as a list with documents, continuation, request_charge and session_token.

  • $read(id, partition_key) reads one document as a named list.

Details

Use oauth_db_cosmos_client() for sign-in. Users need Cosmos DB data-plane roles, such as Cosmos DB Built-in Data Reader, scoped to the database or container. Azure subscription roles alone don't grant data access. Other Cosmos DB APIs and account administration aren't supported.

Create the client inside server(). Each operation stays bound to the authorization that started it and gets a current token for every page. Results arriving after account replacement or sign-out are discarded. Read requests may refresh and retry once after HTTP 401. Throttling and other errors stop the operation; no account key or host credentials are used.

Queries and partitions

Use named parameters without @, such as list(country = "NL") for SQL containing @country. Values can be JSON scalars, arrays or objects; NULL becomes JSON null. Dates and timestamps use ISO strings.

With partition_key = NULL, queries enable cross-partition execution. Supply a scalar key to select one partition, or an unnamed list of up to three components for a hierarchical key. list(NULL) selects a null key. This selects data; it doesn't restrict the visitor's database permissions. Some cross-partition query plans need the vendor SDK's result merging; this client sends the query to the REST gateway without rewriting it.

Results and pagination

Object projections become columns. Missing and null fields become NA in scalar columns; nested or mixed values stay in list columns. Scalar or mixed SELECT VALUE results use a value list column. Large JSON integers stay as strings. Empty results have no field schema.

raw = TRUE returns the collected native documents, total request_charge and last session_token, with continuation = NULL. A missing request-charge header produces NA_real_. $query_page() preserves nested documents and nulls. Reuse its continuation and session token only with the same query, parameters, partition and account.

Queries are synchronous and collect results in memory. Use $query_page() for larger results. Session tokens are carried between pages of one operation, never cached across accounts or independent operations.

See also

oauth_db_cosmos_client(). vignette("cosmos", package = "shinyOAuthDB") has registration and role setup.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
cosmos <- oauth_db_cosmos_api(
  auth$connection, url = "https://example.documents.azure.com",
  database = "reporting", container = "orders"
)
output$rows <- shiny::renderTable({
  cosmos$query(
    "SELECT c.id, c.total FROM c WHERE c.country = @country",
    parameters = list(country = "NL"), partition_key = "NL"
  )
})
} # }
